events.title: Richard III Becomes King of England
events.description: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, took the throne as Richard III. He did so after Parliament-backed claims that his young nephew, Edward V, was illegitimate.
events.significance: His brief reign ended at Bosworth Field in 1485. That battle ended the Plantagenet dynasty and brought the Tudors to power.

events.title: United Nations Charter Signed in San Francisco
events.description: Delegates from 50 nations signed the founding charter of the United Nations. The ceremony took place at the end of a two-month conference.
events.significance: The charter created the main international body for peace, security and cooperation after World War II. It remains central to world diplomacy.

events.title: Kennedy's 'Ich bin ein Berliner' Speech
events.description: U.S. President John F. Kennedy spoke to huge crowds in West Berlin. He declared his solidarity with the city's residents, who lived surrounded by Communist East Germany.
events.significance: The speech became one of the best-known moments of the Cold War. It symbolized American commitment to defending freedom in Europe.

events.title: First Barcode Scanned at a Supermarket
events.description: A cashier at a supermarket in Troy, Ohio, scanned a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum. It was the first retail item sold using a Universal Product Code.
events.significance: The barcode transformed retail and logistics. It made checkout faster and inventory tracking far more accurate.

events.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone Is Published
events.description: J. K. Rowling's first Harry Potter novel was released in the United Kingdom by Bloomsbury. Its first print run was small.
events.significance: The book launched one of the best-selling book series ever. It also spawned a global film and media franchise.
